8821185.title: Dungka!
8821185.extract:
# Dungka!

Dungka! (stylized in all caps with an exclamation mark) is a Filipino-language song by the Manila-based P-pop group SB19, released on April 25, 2025 as one of the focus tracks of their third extended play (EP), Simula at Wakas, under Sony Music Entertainment and 1Z Entertainment . Written by SB19 leader John Paulo “Pablo” Nase and produced with his brother Josue under their RadKidz moniker, the track transforms the everyday Filipino phrase “doon ka” (“go over there”) into a playful, assertive refrain aimed at brushing off negativity . A six-minute music video directed by Kerbs Balagtas of YouMeUs MNL depicts vibrant scenes of urban Philippine life and features high-profile cameos from artists and creators including Vice Ganda, Maymay Entrata, Alodia Gosiengfiao, Sassa Gurl, Kween Yasmin, Pat Lasaten and Agnes Reoma of Ben&Ben, Mimiyuuuh, and others . 

The song received significant coverage from major newspapers and trade and culture publications—such as The Philippine Star, Inquirer Entertainment, Billboard Philippines, Bandwagon Asia, Nylon Manila, Daily Tribune, and VMAN SEA—highlighting its cultural specificity, themes of community and self-expression, and its maximalist, rave-influenced sound . Commercially, Dungka! debuted at No. 7 on Billboard’s World Digital Song Sales chart and entered the Billboard Philippines Hot 100 at No. 21 . It won Pop Song of the Year at the inaugural Filipino Music Awards in 2025 and also secured People’s Choice Song of the Year, among SB19’s six wins at the event . A separate collaboration music video with Japanese game developer SNK ties the track to Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves, integrating the game’s “REV IT UP” slogan with SB19’s choreography and performance .

## Background and recording

Dungka! appears on Simula at Wakas, the final EP in SB19’s trilogy that began with Pagsibol (2021) and continued with Pagtatag (2023). The release contextualizes the group’s personal and artistic journey, exploring closure, renewal, and the finite nature of time and fame . SB19 and their longtime collaborators describe the EP’s aesthetic as balancing familiar P-pop terrain with experimentation; Dungka! was framed as one of the set’s “focus tracks” . 

The track was written by Pablo (John Paulo Nase). Production, mixing, and mastering were handled by RadKidz, the tandem of Pablo and his brother Josue, as credited on the official music video . The EP was released globally through Sony Music Entertainment in partnership with SB19’s management company, 1Z Entertainment .

## Composition and lyrics

Dungka! is characterized by pounding, rave-influenced and hyper-pop elements, aggressive rhythmic accents, and swaggering rap verses from Pablo and Josh, reflecting a maximalist pop approach within the group’s evolving sound palette . Lyrically, the title phrase pivots on Filipino wordplay—turning “doon ka” (“go over there”) into a spirited directive to step aside—framed as a cheeky dismissal of detractors and negative energy. In passages like “Tumabi ka! Kung ‘di mo ‘to gusto” (“Step aside! If you don’t like this”), the song asserts agency while inviting communal revelry . 

Coverage emphasized Pablo’s preference for wordplay and the track’s loud-yet-catchy production, situating Dungka! as a playful rejoinder to critics and a celebration of SB19’s diverse identities and influences .

## Music video

The official music video for Dungka! was released on April 25, 2025 and directed by Kerbs Balagtas (YouMeUs MNL). It interweaves scenes of everyday Filipino street and pop culture—sari-sari stores, street-food stalls, jeepneys, karaoke, pickup basketball, Zumba, ten-twenty (Chinese garter), and protest rallies—creating a kinetic portrait of urban Manila . 

The video features a wide array of cameos selected to align with its message of diversity, pride, and collective action: Vice Ganda, Maymay Entrata, Alodia Gosiengfiao, Sassa Gurl, Kween Yasmin, Malupiton, Ghost Wrecker, Shehyee, Smugglaz, Ben&Ben’s Pat Lasaten and Agnes Reoma, Mimiyuuuh, and Jayat, among others . Visual motifs include placards advocating Filipino arts (“Iangat ang sining na Pilipino”) and a poster stating “Sining Ang Sandata sa Kulturang Mapagpalaya” (“Art is the weapon of a liberating culture”) pasted over a traditional politician’s signage—read by coverage as social critique embedded in a street-party tableau . 

Independent features praised the MV’s generous celebration of ordinary Filipino life, its dense references and “Easter eggs,” and the decision to embed SB19 within the community rather than centering them above it .

## Release and promotion

Simula at Wakas and the Dungka! music video were released on April 25, 2025 . On the same day, SB19 staged surprise flash mob performances in Bonifacio Global City (Taguig), performing Dungka! alongside the pre-release single Dam near a temporary “Dam Tree” public art installation . Shortly afterward, SB19 performed at Xiaomi’s All-Star Summer Concert at Enchanted Kingdom in Sta. Rosa, Laguna, where Dungka! was introduced as a surprise new track . The group promoted the song in multiple live formats, including a Wish 107.5 Stopover Sessions performance and their debut episode on Billboard Philippines Studios, where Dungka! closed a three-song set from Simula at Wakas . 

Dungka! has been a regular feature of SB19’s Simula at Wakas World Tour set list, including the two-night kickoff at Philippine Arena (Bulacan) on May 31 and June 1, 2025 . Inquirer Entertainment and Bandwagon Asia also covered the group’s cross-cultural collaboration with SNK for Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves, releasing a cinematic music video built around Dungka! and the game’s “REV IT UP” tagline , as formally announced by SNK in a May 26, 2025 press release .

## Reception

Significant coverage in major Philippine outlets and regional culture media framed Dungka! as a sonically bold and culturally anchored work. VMAN SEA described the six-minute MV as “a joyful portrait of Filipino life” that refuses to dilute its local specificity, noting Pablo’s transformation of “doon ka” into a defiant, communal refrain . Inquirer POP! highlighted the video’s social messages, political undertones, and queerness-affirming cameos, interpreting scenes (such as a crab-eating antagonist) as commentary on “crab mentality” and cancel culture . Daily Tribune emphasized the MV’s energetic depiction of Manila street life and its celebrity-packed cast . Bandwagon Asia described the song’s sound as “experimental hyper-pop/rave-influenced maximalism” within the EP’s ecosystem . Billboard Philippines contextualized Dungka! within SB19’s evolving performance repertoire, including its Studios feature and use on the world tour, while extensively documenting the EP’s chart impact . 

Audience engagement was reflected in widely covered dance challenges and collaborative clips, with Inquirer POP! reporting on creators joining the Dungka! dance trend . Across outlets, the prevailing view holds that Dungka! merges diss track swagger and local references with an inclusive call to community and self-expression .

## Accolades

- Filipino Music Awards (FMAs), October 21, 2025:
 - Pop Song of the Year — Dungka! 
 - People’s Choice Song of the Year — Dungka! 
- SB19 won a total of six FMAs at the inaugural ceremony, including Artist of the Year, Tour of the Year, and Concert of the Year, with multiple sources emphasizing the event’s industry significance and SB19’s dominant showing .

## Commercial performance

- Billboard World Digital Song Sales (U.S.): Debuted at No. 7 (week reported by Inquirer Entertainment on May 6, 2025; contextualized by Forbes) . 
- Billboard Philippines Hot 100: Entered at No. 21 for the chart dated May 10, 2025 (Chart Beat report) .

## Track context

Dungka! is one of the seven tracks on Simula at Wakas, alongside Dam, Time, Quit, 8TonBall, Shooting for the Stars, and an extended version of Dam. The EP release and related activations (including the Dam Tree installation in Bonifacio Global City) were covered by The Philippine Star and Bandwagon Asia .

## Personnel

Credits per the official music video and release coverage:
- SB19 — performers 
- Writer — John Paulo “Pablo” Nase 
- Producers, mixing, mastering — RadKidz (Pablo and Josue) 
- Music video director — Kerbs Balagtas (YouMeUs MNL) 
- Featured video cameos — Vice Ganda; Maymay Entrata; Alodia Gosiengfiao; Sassa Gurl; Kween Yasmin; Malupiton; Ghost Wrecker; Shehyee; Smugglaz; Pat Lasaten and Agnes Reoma (Ben&Ben); Mimiyuuuh; Jayat; among others 

## Legacy and cultural impact

Coverage frequently characterizes Dungka! as an archival snapshot of contemporary Filipino street culture, asserting that leaning into local specificity can broaden resonance. VMAN SEA argued that the video “refuses to sand down cultural particularities,” and that specificity is what allows universality . Inquirer POP! highlighted how the MV’s messaging—art, politics, queer pride, and community solidarity—connected during an election season and sparked detailed viewer interpretation, reinforcing SB19’s role in cultural discourse . The SNK collaboration introduced Dungka! to gaming audiences regionally, emphasizing cross-media reach and SB19’s international partnerships .

## Controversies

No major controversies were widely reported in reliable sources regarding the song or its music video. Interpretive coverage discussed the MV’s depictions of “crab mentality,” political posters, and social critique; these were framed as artistic choices rather than points of public controversy .

## Other uses of the title

Searches identified non-musical uses of “Dungka” (without the exclamation mark) in retail branding and e-commerce contexts, including a lifestyle brand referencing a Himalayan conch-shell etymology. These are unrelated to SB19’s Dungka! and are noted only to distinguish them from the song [Note: example brand page] [Optional].

- Simula at Wakas — SB19 EP featuring Dungka! 
- Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves — SNK fighting game featured in the collaboration MV

1.title: SB19 drops 3rd EP 'Simula at Wakas,' ‘Dungka’ MV features Vice Ganda, Maymay Entrata

SB19 drops 3rd EP 'Simula at Wakas,' ‘Dungka’ MV features Vice Ganda, Maymay Entrata
====================================================================================

[Kathleen A. Llemit](https://www.philstar.com/authors/1807004/kathleen-a-llemit) - Philstar.com

April 25, 2025 | 5:30pm

[![Image 18: A 25x24 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://media.philstar.com/assets/icons/stroke-12-grey-comment.png)](https://www.philstar.com/entertainment/music/2025/04/25/2438329/sb19-drops-3rd-ep-simula-wakas-dungka-mv-features-vice-ganda-maymay-entrata#comments)

![Image 19: SB19 drops 3rd EP 'Simula at Wakas,' â��Dungkaâ�� MV features Vice Ganda, Maymay Entrata](https://media.philstar.com/photos/2025/04/25/sb19-dungka-final_2025-04-25_17-47-48.jpg)

P-pop group SB19 releases the music video for 'Dungka,' featuring star-studded appearances led by Vice Ganda, on April 25, 2025, in time for the release of its third extended play 'Simula at Wakas.'

Sony Music Entertainment / Released

ADVERTISEMENT

MANILA, Philippines — P-pop group SB19 served three surprises today by dropping the music videos of their two singles, “Dungka” and “Time,” from their just released third extended play (EP) “Simula at Wakas,” with star-studded appearances led by box-office star Vice Ganda.

“Dungka” is yet another testament to the songwriting skills and preference for wordplay of leader Pablo, credited with his real name John Paulo Nase. He produced and mixed the single with his brother Josue, the duo collectively called RadKidz.

“Dungka” slides out of the mouth of the quintet as a way of shooing unwanted personalities, just like how Filipinos would utter “doon ka (move away or out)” to show displeasure.

With rap lines by Josh and Pablo in the middle of the track and a music video that features the chaotic energy of urban Manila, “Dungka” is a statement song with a catchy beat.

Vice Ganda, Maymay Entrata, Alodia Gosiengfiao, Sassa Gurl, Kween Yasmin, Ben&Ben’s Pat Lasaten and Agnes Reoma, and Mimiyuuuh lend credence to the diversity and self-expression message of “Dungka.”

“Time,” meanwhile, is a more somber MV, a contrast to “Dungka.” It similar to mellow and instrospective songs by SB19, with composition and lyrics by Pablo. Xerxes Bakker also wrote and composed the lyrics. Samuel Akinbode also contributed to its lyrics.

SB19’s “Simula at Wakas” is the final EP in the trilogy of past albums, “Pagsibol” (2021) and “Pagtatag” (2023).

The P-pop group will kick-off its “Simula at Wakas” world tour with a two-day show on May 31 and June 1 at the Philippine Arena in Bulacan.

P-pop kings SB19 have released the [music video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SO-G0WMzSdo) for “DUNGKA!” but it’s more than just that—it highlights important themes that are highly relevant today.

Throughout the video, Filipino culture is showcased, featuring elements commonly seen in the Philippines, such as sari-sari stores, jeepneys on the streets, and traveling stalls where people can buy street food, just to name a few.

This song is clapping back at those bashers/naysayers who are doubting their capabilities as artists. In a certain scene, content creator Ghost Wrecker is acting as the basher walking down the street while the P-pop kings paid no attention to him and just continued doing what they were working on.

There was also a particular scene wherein he was eating crabs that can be a symbolism of Filipinos having crab mentality wherein they pull others down.

With lines like “Tumabi ka! Kung ‘di mo ‘to gusto \[Step aside! If you don’t like this\]” and “Tumabi ka diyan \[Move out of the way\]!” it is certain that they are telling them to just back off.

Along with clapping back to the bashers, they have taken this opportunity to raise social awareness as there are several people in the music video having signs like “Iangat ang sining na Pilipino” and with SB19 Justin seen in another shot wherein he is placing a “Sining Ang Sandata sa Kulturang Mapagpalaya” poster over a trapo poster.

Furthermore, it is a colorful tribute to LGBTQIA+ artists who continue to inspire with pride and authenticity. Sassa Gurl, Pat Laseten and Agnes Reoma from Ben&Ben, Mimiyuuuh, and Vice Ganda are just some of the artists who are part of the community featured in the video.

Upon seeing the music video, people then took to social media to share their thoughts.

One user wrote, “The Power. The Message. The Energy. Dungka isn’t just fun & full of life. The MV shows our Filipino culture, the nasty and the good. How some thrive in bringing people down and how we rise to it through togetherness to amplify the message SB19 has long been telling everyone.”

“Did they just walk passed that guy who was like the metaphor for the bashers and doubters and said, “TUMABI KA DYAN??”(we have bigger problems dude), then pans the vid to that politician?????? ART. SPEAKS. INDEED,” a second user wrote.

A third user wrote, “EVERYTHING !! IS !! POLITICAL !! Sobrang timely rin na nilabas ‘tong MV ng dungka ngayong election season \[It’s very timely that they released the dungka MV this election season. VOTE WISELY, GUYS!!!”

> Now we understand the significance of the star-studded lineup in the DUNGKA MV. It goes beyond SB19 simply responding to haters and bashers; this message resonates with everyone—celebrities, influencers, and everyday people alike.

![Image 32: SB19 teams up with ‘Fatal Fury’ gamemakers for new ‘DUNGKA!’ video. Image: Handout photo](https://entertainment.inquirer.net/files/2025/05/SNK___________SB19-2.jpg)SB19 and Japanese gaming company SNK Corporation joined forces for an exciting collaboration. Image: Handout photo

**[SB19](https://entertainment.inquirer.net/609268/sb19s-dungka-enters-billboards-world-digital-song-sales-chart)** expanded their global reach by collaborating with Japanese gaming and entertainment company SNK Corporation for a new music video of “DUNGKA!” featuring the latter’s game “Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves.”

The P-pop powerhouse and SNK’s collaboration was announced in a press statement on Monday, May 26, noting that it combines SB19’s “genre-defying sound” and the “cinematic battle sequences” of “Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves.”

_Article continues after this advertisement_

The music video features Pablo, Josh, Stell, Ken, and Justin interacting with the camera and performing “DUNGKA!” at a recording booth and dance studio, while scenes of the video game are alternately shown.

SB19’s ‘DUNGKA!’ Is a Joyful Portrait of Filipino Life—And a Sharp Middle Finger To Negativity
==============================================================================================

In a luminous swirl of street life, protest chants, and sticky-sweet nostalgia, _DUNGKA!_ captures the defiant heartbeat of a nation refusing to stand still

By [Dayne Aduna](https://vman-sea.com/author/dayne-aduna/ "Posts by Dayne Aduna")

April 26, 2025

[![Image 4: Facebook](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/facebook.svg)](https://www.addtoany.com/add_to/facebook?linkurl=https%3A%2F%2Fvman-sea.com%2Farts-culture%2Fmusic%2Fsb19s-dungka-is-a-joyful-portrait-of-filipino-life-and-a-sharp-middle-finger-to-negativity%2F&linkname=SB19%E2%80%99s%20%26%238216%3BDUNGKA%21%26%238217%3B%20Is%20a%20Joyful%20Portrait%20of%20Filipino%20Life%E2%80%94And%20a%20Sharp%20Middle%20Finger%20To%20Negativity "Facebook")[![Image 5: Instagram](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/instagram.svg)](https://www.instagram.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvman-sea.com%2Farts-culture%2Fmusic%2Fsb19s-dungka-is-a-joyful-portrait-of-filipino-life-and-a-sharp-middle-finger-to-negativity%2F "Instagram")[![Image 6: X](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/x.svg)](https://www.instagram.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvman-sea.com%2Farts-culture%2Fmusic%2Fsb19s-dungka-is-a-joyful-portrait-of-filipino-life-and-a-sharp-middle-finger-to-negativity%2F "X")[![Image 7: Email](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/email.svg)](https://www.instagram.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvman-sea.com%2Farts-culture%2Fmusic%2Fsb19s-dungka-is-a-joyful-portrait-of-filipino-life-and-a-sharp-middle-finger-to-negativity%2F "Email")[![Image 8: Copy Link](https://vman-sea.com/wp-content/themes/vman/addtoany/icons/link.svg)](https://www.instagram.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvman-sea.com%2Farts-culture%2Fmusic%2Fsb19s-dungka-is-a-joyful-portrait-of-filipino-life-and-a-sharp-middle-finger-to-negativity%2F "Copy Link")

  ![Image 9: sb19 DUNGKA!](https://b3720787.smushcdn.com/3720787/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/sb19-dungka-banner.webp?lossy=2&strip=1&webp=1)

A soundtrack for defiance and joy
---------------------------------

It was only fitting that SB19—the luminary architects of P-pop’s current renaissance—graced the cover of our [Spring 2025 issue](https://vman-sea.com/on-the-cover/sb19-the-brotherhood-behind-the-music-and-why-theyre-stronger-than-ever/). Even then, they seemed poised on the brink of another breakthrough, and with the release of the _DUNGKA!_ music video, they have, once again, pushed beyond the expected.

_DUNGKA!_ is a six-minute exhale of Filipino life: vivid, messy, and magnetic. The music video stitches together a tapestry of the archipelago’s pulse—street basketball courts alive with sweaty, frenetic games; vendors hawking _kwek-kwek_ and _isaw_; karaoke sessions conducted in cracked plastic chairs; Zumba in parking lots; children hopping between chalk squares in 10-20; rally banners flapping against concrete and sky. Election campaigns roar in the background, as much a fixture of the landscape as the sunset-lit jeepneys rattling down narrow streets. Every frame hums with the particular, chaotic beauty of ordinary days in the Philippines.

And threaded through it all, like a live wire: SB19, effortless in their command, moving not above the scenes, but through them.

_ALSO READ: [FELIP’s Meteoric Rise](https://vman-sea.com/arts-culture/music/felips-meteoric-rise/)_

Staying stubbornly, brilliantly local
-------------------------------------

Musically, _DUNGKA!_— produced by Pablo and his brother Josue under their RadKidz moniker—is a rave-fueled masterstroke. Over a pounding beat, Pablo and Josh trade bold rap verses, their delivery swaggering and infectious. Pablo’s wordplay turns the everyday Filipino phrase “_doon ka_” (“go over there”) into a playful, defiant refrain—a winking incantation to repel bad vibes, dead weight, and unwanted forces.

Advertisement

The effect is both jubilant and cutting. If the song is an invitation to join the revelry, it is also a gatekeeping spell: only those who belong, who understand, may stay.

      ![Image 10: sb19](https://b3720787.smushcdn.com/3720787/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/VMAN-SB19-2.jpg?lossy=2&strip=1&webp=1)

on josh, pablo, ken, and stell:  
all clothing _**tod’s**_ / jewelry _**bvlgari**_

—

on justin:

all clothing _**brunello cucinelli**_ / jewelry _**bvlgari**_

Yet beyond its aesthetic bravado and sonic innovation, _DUNGKA!_ is significant because it refuses to dilute itself. It is deeply and stubbornly local, packed with references that demand fluency, but offered generously enough to welcome newcomers. It is a pop star flex, but also an archival act: a documentation of how Filipinos live, love, eat, protest, and endure.

In an era when many artists aspire to cross borders by sanding down their cultural particularities, SB19 does the opposite. They dig deeper. And somehow, in doing so, they make their music—and their movement—feel not just national, but planetary.

Advertisement

After all, specificity is what makes universality possible. In the chaotic beauty of _DUNGKA!_, SB19 reminds us that the more vividly you show your own world, the more the world will want to see.

Osaka, Japan — SNK today unveiled a music video collaboration with acclaimed Filipino boy band SB19 for its new fighting game FATAL FURY: City of the Wolves.

[![Image 1](https://www.snk-corp.co.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/sb19_wducgwk.jpg)](https://www.snk-corp.co.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/sb19_wducgwk.jpg)

### Pinoy pop meets furious fighting action! New music video for SB19’s “DUNGKA!” specially crafted around CotW’s call to REV IT UP!

The tagline “REV IT UP” from FATAL FURY: City of the Wolves guided the creation of this collaborative music video for SB19’s new song “DUNGKA!”, pairing the group’s distinctive rhythm and dance with the heart-pounding action of fighting games. See how this exciting endeavor turned out below!

**＞****FATAL FURY: CotW × SB19****｜****Collaboration Music Video**

[https://youtu.be/L3AWQN40nvM](https://youtu.be/L3AWQN40nvM)

[![Image 2](https://www.snk-corp.co.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/sb19_xqycss.jpg)](https://www.snk-corp.co.jp/wp/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/sb19_xqycss.jpg)

**SB19 Profile**

SB19 is a five-member Filipino boy band who has built a dedicated global following in less than three years since their official launch. The quintet—composed of Pablo, Josh, Stell, Ken, and Justin— debuted in October 2018 with their first single “Tilaluha,” the award-winning group paved the way for Pinoy-Pop (P-Pop) to gain worldwide acclaim, while breaking new ground in terms of integrating modern pop/hip-hop/electronic music with homegrown sensibilities.

SB19 has continued to ascend international charts, breaking barriers as the first Filipino act to be nominated for a Billboard Music Award in 2021. Their dedication and innovation culminated in notable projects including their critically acclaimed EP, “Pagsibol” (2021), and their groundbreaking single “Bazinga,” which topped Billboard’s Hot Trending Songs chart, underscoring their global impact and growing international fandom. In 2023, SB19 further solidified their presence on the world stage with the release of their EP “PAGTATAG!,” which featured hits like “GENTO,” marking their first top 10 placement on Billboard’s World Digital Song Sales chart. The release of “PAGTATAG!” also marked the group’s transition to self-management under their own label, 1Z Entertainment, offering greater creative freedom and artistic control. Their highly successful PAGTATAG! World Tour included sold-out shows across the Philippines, United States, and Canada, and “GENTO” was officially approved as an entry for the 66th Annual Grammy Awards.

By 2025, SB19 released their long awaited comeback with the EP “Simula at Wakas” starting things strong with “DAM”. The track garnered records and chart success both locally and internationally with it reaching the IFPI top 20 spots in the Philippines, Middle East and Hong Kong and No. 1 in the Billboard World Digital Song Sales Charts in its 1st week of release.

**What is FATAL FURY: City of the Wolves?**

SNK’s beloved _Fatal Fury_ series first hit the market in 1991, spearheading the fighting game boom of the 1990s that swept the industry thereafter. GAROU: MARK OF THE WOLVES (released in 1999) has, for some time, served as the franchise’s most recent installment. But that is all about to change: 26 years on, a brand-new entry—**FATAL FURY: City of the Wolves**—has arrived on the scene!

FATAL FURY: City of the Wolves features a unique art style that stimulates the senses, an innovative REV System that supercharges the excitement, plus a host of other battle systems even more robust than before. The game also breathes new life into the series by introducing two distinct control schemes (ensuring fun and excitement for newcomers and veterans alike) as well as other fresh features and elements.

The streets of South Town are a hotbed of action, wild dreams, and even wilder ambition. Here, at long last, a new legend is about to unfold…

![Image 1: SB19 releases phenomenal finale of EP trilogy 'Simula at Wakas' alongside poignant music video for 'DUNGKA!' & 'Time'](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/crop=d:%5B0%2C1539%2C7789%2C3894%5D/resize=w:1920/pjpg=q:90/compress/MYZGnE4tSiegxL7nygUO)

Celebrating a journey marked by shared experience, invaluable wisdom, and artistic growth, **SB19** returns with the release of their third EP, **_Simula at Wakas_**—out on all digital music platforms worldwide via **Sony Music Entertainment**. Their highly anticipated body of work captures the band’s evolution as artists and individuals, honoring the past while stepping boldly into the future.

“It’s our way of saying thank you and showing how much we’ve evolved,” P-pop kings share in an official statement. “_Simula at Wakas_ encapsulates everything we’ve been through: the struggles, the growth, the milestones. We hope it speaks not only to those who’ve been with us from the start but also welcomes new listeners into our world.”

As the final installment in a trilogy that began with 2021’s **_pagsibol_** and 2023’s **_PAGTATAG!_**, _Simula at Wakas_ chronicles the Filipino pop group’s artistic and personal transformation while signaling a bold, forward-looking direction. The EP explores the universal themes of closure and renewal, portraying the life of an artist as they navigate fame, pressure, and identity. The band further shared personal anecdotes and reflections on their journey to _Simula at Wakas_ in the _**This is SB19**_ playlist on Spotify.

The P-pop trailblazers explain, “It’s both a celebration of our journey so far and a declaration of what’s to come. We’re the same group as when we started. It's just that we’ve matured, evolved, and grown into artists who are more confident in our voice and purpose.”

_Simula at Wakas_ showcases the 'DAM' hitmakers' captivating and universally relatable sound, all while remaining true to their values as human beings. From emotionally resonant lyrics to innovative, genre-bending soundscapes, the EP offers a meaningful experience that is sure to leave a lasting impression.

The release is written and produced by SB19 with their trusted pool of international and local collaborators, including **Xerxes Bakker**, **Alawn**, **August Rigo**, **Simon Servida**, and **Josue (RADKIDZ)**. The EP features the full creative involvement of all five members. SB19 admits that they took a hands-on approach in shaping every aspect of the project and were very deliberate in contributing not just musically but also creatively—from the narrative of each track to its visual interpretation, from the choreography to music videos.

“We held meetings almost every day to carefully discuss how each song would come together, from conceptualizing and message to planning how we could execute and promote the EP in ways we’ve never done before,” SB19 explains. “This is the first time after how many years that every member has been this hands-on. Everyone was involved in conceptualizing, producing, and writing the songs. But we also owe a lot to our collaborators who helped us push our ideas further and elevate the project on both the technical and creative sides.”

The envelope-pushing EP cements their position as one of the vital forces behind contemporary pop music in the Philippines and Southeast Asia for the last decade, providing a riveting insight into less explored paths and a thrilling outlook for future developments. _Simula at Wakas_ contains seven songs, including the now-viral single **'DAM'** alongside the focus tracks **'DUNGKA!'** and **'Time'**.

The anthemic ballad 'Time' essays the inevitability of time’s passing—an undeniable and unavoidable reality. As the lyrics go, “One day we’ll run out of time,” the song reveals a sobering reminder of life’s impermanence, yet one that inspires purpose and presence. “Hindi naman kami forever SB19,” acknowledges the five-piece act. “Nothing is permanent in this world, even from where we are at this point. Time will run out soon. All we can do is try our best and make the most out it.”

'DUNGKA!', another focus track, vaults SB19 back to their experimental phase: evangelizing pop music in unrecognizably exciting form and embracing maximalist production with rave and hyper-pop elements. It’s easily one of the biggest surprises of the EP, standing its ground as both a sonic rebel and revelation.

To complement the EP’s release, SB19 introduces the **DAM Tree**, an immersive public art installation, now open to the public in Bonifacio Global City (BGC) until 4 May. As part of the promotional campaign, fans can experience the world of **Simula at Wakas** through hanging parabolic sound domes where **A’TIN** first heard exclusive track previews from the EP. Beyond the immersive listening experience, visitors also get the chance to win exciting prizes, quickly becoming a hotspot for fan frenzy.

“A tree, by nature, reflects life’s different stages, starting from a seed, growing roots, eventually branching out and bearing,” the group explains. “That aligns with the message of 'DAM' and the EP as a whole: acknowledging where we began, embracing how we’ve evolved, and looking ahead to what’s next. The DAM Tree is not just a design; it’s an experience. We wanted people to feel connected to the music in a more immersive way. It’s our way of turning the emotions behind Simula at Wakas into something you can actually see and feel.”

Further solidifying this milestone, SB19 will kick off the [_**Simula at Wakas World Tour**_](https://www.bandwagon.asia/articles/sb19-sell-out-simula-at-wakas-world-tour-stops-in-record-time-announce-singapore-leg-in-august) with two landmark concerts at the iconic **Philippine Arena** on 31 May and 1 June, with the first one already sold out. The tour will span across major cities in Taiwan, the United States, Canada, Singapore, and the Middle East from June to October this year, with additional stops in Australia, Japan, and Hong Kong to be announced.

“We’ve been working on new arrangements for some of our songs, and we’re really excited for fans to hear them,” the group shares. “We’ll be performing tracks from our latest EP, _Simula at Wakas_, and we can’t wait to share the energy and emotion behind each song. Every performance has been thoughtfully prepared, and we’re really looking forward to seeing how our fans react to these new versions of our music. Each day will be a different experience!”

ADVERTISEMENT

MANILA, Philippines — P-pop group SB19 performed their new tracks at the Xiaomi All-Star Summer Concert in Enchanted Kingdom, Sta Rosa, Laguna.

SB19 undoubtedly had the crowd roaring with their dynamic choreography and catchy tunes. Their set featured songs from their newest EP (extended play), "Simula at Wakas."

They kicked it off with an electrifying performance of “DAM,” followed by the emotional ballad “Time,” which they performed onstage for the first time.

Before the night ended, they surprised the crowd with their new track “Dungka!”

SB19 played a fun guessing game, where they had to decipher the images and emojis symbolizing Redmi Note 14’s iconic features. The crowd also enjoyed answering the questions with the P-Pop group.

After that, SB19 drew the three lucky winners of the all-new Redmi Note 14 Pro+ 5G in Sand Gold.

“There’s no better way to commemorate 15 great years of making innovation accessible to all our Xiaomi fans by paying back their loyalty with a grand celebration like the Xiaomi All Star Summer Concert. We look forward to many more exciting years of innovations and a complete digital lifestyle for the Philippines,” said Tomi Adrias, Xiaomi Philippines Head of Marketing.

SB19’s “Dungka!” debuts at No. 7 on Billboard’s World Digital Song Sales chart, giving the group another top 10 hit from Simula at Wakas. BULACAN, PHILIPPINES - DECEMBER 14: Pablo, Stell, Ken, Justin, and Josh of boy group SB19 attend the 2023 Asia Artist Awards at the Philippine Arena on December 14, 2023 in Bulacan, Philippines. (Photo by Ezra Acayan/Getty Images)... More

Getty Images

SB19 has been one of the hottest musical acts in the Philippines for several years now, and certainly among the top-performing commercially. While the boy band began expanding outside the Asian nation with its past project, the last few months have been especially significant, as the outfit’s new short album _Simula at Wakas_ shows that the misicians have absolutely developed an audience in Western markets, such as the United States.

Another single spun off from the band’s new EP has not only become a commercial success in America, but a top 10 smash for the vocal troupe – another one.

**“Dungka!” Debuts on** _**Billboard’s**_ **World Digital Song Sales Chart**
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

[“Dungka!”](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SO-G0WMzSdo) debuts on the World Digital Song Sales chart this week. The cut launches at No. 7 on the purchase-centric tally. [SB19](https://www.google.com/url?sa=t&source=web&rct=j&opi=89978449&url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/hughmcintyre/2025/05/08/sb19-charts-its-first-album-in-a-major-music-market/&ved=2ahUKEwjkz8GGhpeNAxUjFlkFHfOjDKkQFnoECBcQAQ&usg=AOvVaw38bXnZMHMAnKh1M0f3AIYF) scores the top start of the week on the 10-spot ranking, and the Filipino boy band’s latest focus track is one of only two new arrivals this time around. The other, “Will Ye Go, Lassie Go,” is credited to Lola Kirke, Peter Dreams, Brian Dunphy, Darren Holden and Jack O'Connell, all of whom are actors (and singers) in the blockbuster movie _Sinners_. That tune enters at No. 10, in last place.

PROMOTED

**SB19 Occupies Multiple Spots on the Chart**
---------------------------------------------

This frame, SB19 fills a pair of positions on the World Digital Song Sales list. As “Dungka!” starts at No. 7, the first single taken from _Simula at Wakas_, “Dam,” kicks off its third week on the ranking, reentering at No. 4. Earlier this year, “Dam” became the group’s first champion on this _Billboard_ tally.

SB19 first appeared on the World Digital Song Sales chart in 2023, making history when “Gento” arrived. That tune spent just one frame at No. 8, earning the group an initial top 10 bestseller.

**SB19 Claims 20% of the Entire List**
--------------------------------------

This week, SB19 claims 20% of all the spots on the World Digital Song Sales ranking. The Filipino male vocal troupe is the only non-solo musical act to occupy more than one position.

SB19’s ‘DUNGKA!’ enters Billboard’s World Digital Song Sales chart

[![Image 26: Bookmark](blob:https://entertainment.inquirer.net/76f70cba1a4985ff842bd808acca549c)](https://entertainment.inquirer.net/609268/sb19s-dungka-enters-billboards-world-digital-song-sales-chart#)

![Image 32: SB19’s ‘Dungka!’ enters Billboard’s World Digital Song Sales chart. Image: X/@SB19Official](https://entertainment.inquirer.net/files/2025/05/SB19-concept-photo-for-Dungka-scaled.jpeg)SB19 members (from left) Josh, Stell, Ken, Justin, and Pablo in a concept photo for “DUNGKA!” Image: X/@SB19Official

“DUNGKA!”, a song from **[SB19](https://entertainment.inquirer.net/607481/for-sb19-simula-at-wakas-is-a-pinnacle-of-their-monumental-efforts)**’s third EP “Simula at Wakas,” has made a strong impression on listeners as it entered Billboard’s World Digital Song Sales chart.

The track made it to Billboard’s World Digital Song Sales chart at the seventh spot, making this their third song to achieve the milestone after “Gento” and “DAM.”

_Article continues after this advertisement_

![Image 34: Image: Screengrab from Billboard's website](blob:https://entertainment.inquirer.net/e2dcf3b1dbee6272bd1b57a37b12b3e6)Image: Screengrab from Billboard’s website

“DUNGKA!”, as well as other songs from the EP such as “DAM,” “Time,” “Quit,” “8TonBall,” “and “Shooting for the Stars,” are also included in Billboard Philippines’ Hot 100 charts. The songs ranked 21st, 13th, 35th, 71st, 73th, and the 86th, respectively.

In an exclusive interview with INQUIRER.net, SB19’s Justin explained that “DUNGKA!” is one of the focus tracks from the third EP, and is an apparent play on the phrase “D’un ka.”

“It’s more of our personal message to people na nanggugulo… maraming nanggugulo sa’tin and sa lahat. Pero \[para\] sa mga hindi gusto ang ginagawa namin, nandyan sila para ubusin ang oras or what \[sa pag-hate\]. Our message for them is kung hindi mo gusto ‘yung ginagawa namin, wag ka na dito. D’un ka na lang,” he said.

(It’s more of our personal message to those who are messing around with us. A lot of people enjoy messing with us and with others. But to those who don’t like what we do, they are there to waste their time hating. Our message for them is, if you don’t like what we’re doing, get out. Stay in your lane.)

The music video was a star-studded affair as it featured Vice Ganda, Maymay Entrata, Alodia Gosiengfiao, Sassa Gurl, Agnes Reoma, Pat Lasaten, and Mimiyuuuh, to name a few.

_Article continues after this advertisement_

![Image 36: YouTube video player](https://entertainment.inquirer.net/609268/sb19s-dungka-enters-billboards-world-digital-song-sales-chart)

“DUNGKA!”, along with other tracks in the “Simula at Wakas” EP, were released in April 2025. The EP marks the end of their EP trilogy, which also consisted of “Pagsibol,” and “Pagtatag!”.

SB19 debuted in October 2018, consisting of Pablo, Josh, Stell, Ken, and Justin. The group is set to kick off their “Simula at Wakas” world tour at the Philippine Arena on May 31 and June 1.

![Image 22: SB19 kicks off 'Simula at Wakas' world tour with sold-out Philippine Arena show](https://media.philstar.com/photos/2025/06/01/sb19concert_2025-06-01_14-29-59.jpg)

P-pop group SB19

SB19 via Instagram

ADVERTISEMENT

MANILA, Philippines — "Kings of P-pop" SB19 successfully kicked off their "Simula at Wakas" world tour at the Philippine Arena last night.

Pablo, Josh, Ken, Stell and Justin opened the concert with "Dam" to the delight of the sold-out crowd.

SB19 also performed their hit songs "What," "Golden Hour," "Dungka," "Creamzone," "Gento," many others.

"A’TIN! We can’t believe we just finished the first day of our 'Simula at Wakas World Tour Kickoff,'" SB19 wrote on Instagram.

"Thank you for filling the arena with your loud cheers and unstoppable energy. This is just the beginning of something great. See you all again tomorrow!" it added.

The concert became emotional when the group performed "Mapa" showing their parents and families on screen.

The group then thanked A'tin performing their song "SLMT" while being elevated off the stage for their final song.

But SB19 emerged on stage performing "Dam" again for its encore, marking the concert's name "Simula at Wakas."

SB19’s "Simula at Wakas" world tour will take them to United States, Singapore, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

The inaugural **Filipino Music Awards 2025**, held on **21 October** at the SM Mall of Asia Arena, marked a historic moment for OPM with a night full of firsts, fanfare, and fiery performances. From veteran icons to next-gen pop royalty, the awards night drew over 500 artists, industry names, and fans—all united in celebrating the evolution of Filipino music.

**SB19** were undeniable scene-stealers, dominating the evening with six major wins including **Artist of the Year**, **Pop Song of the Year** for **‘Dungka!’**, **Tour of the Year**, **Concert of the Year**, and two fan-voted trophies: **People’s Choice Artist** and **People’s Choice Song**. Fellow crowd-favourite **Cup of Joe** had their own moment in the spotlight, winning **Song of the Year** with **‘Multo’** and **Album of the Year** for **_Silakbo_**.

The FMAs also championed genre diversity, awarding standout acts across alternative, rock, hip-hop, R&B, and folk. **Zild** picked up **Alternative Song of the Year** for **‘I.N.A.S.’**, **IV of Spades** bagged **Rock Song of the Year** with **‘Aura’**, and **Morobeats** won **Hip-Hop Song of the Year** for the powerful **‘Gubat na Siyudad’**. On the R&B front, **Denise Julia** scored with **‘Lackin’**, while **Ben&Ben**’s **‘Dear’** won **Folk Song of the Year**.

Performances were just as memorable. **IV of Spades** electrified the stage with **‘Aura’**, **BGYO** brought arena-level choreography, and **Gloc-9** lit up the arena with **‘Upuan’**. **BINI** fired up the crowd with a slick performance of **‘First Luv’**, while **Ben&Ben** and **SB19** united for a powerful rendition of **‘Kapangyarihan’**. **Ely Buendia** also made a wonderful live appearance with a moving performance of **‘Kandarapa’**. **apl.de.ap** turned things global with a fiery take on **‘WIND IT!’**, and **Cup of Joe** delivered a moving sing-along with **‘Multo’**.

The night also honoured legends: **Pilita Corrales** received the **Tribute Award**, **Jose Mari Chan** was awarded **Lifetime Achievement**, and **Ang Misyon Orchestra** was named **Music Foundation of the Year**.

The FMAs showed that OPM is entering a bold new era—genre-inclusive, globally ready, and powered by a passionate fanbase. It’s not just a celebration, it’s a launchpad.

### Full Winners List

**Artist of the Year**

*   SB19
    

**Song of the Year**

*   ‘Multo’ – Cup of Joe
    

**Album of the Year**

*   _Silakbo_ – Cup of Joe
    

**Pop Song of the Year**

*   ‘Dungka!’ – SB19
    

**Alternative Song of the Year**

*   ‘I.N.A.S.’ – Zild
    

**Rock Song of the Year**

*   ‘Aura’ – IV of Spades
    

**Hip-Hop Song of the Year**

*   ‘Gubat na Siyudad’ – Morobeats
    

**R&B Song of the Year**

*   ‘Lackin’ – Denise Julia
    

**Folk Song of the Year**

*   ‘Dear’ – Ben&Ben
    

**People’s Choice Artist**

*   SB19
    

**People’s Choice Song**

*   ‘Dungka!’ – SB19
    

**Concert of the Year**

23.title: U0IxOSBNYWtlIEhpc3RvcnkgV2l0aCBUd28gTmlnaHRzIEF0IFRoZSBQaGlsaXBwaW5lIEFyZW5h
23.content:
P-pop wouldn’t be where it is today without [SB19](https://billboardphilippines.com/tag/SB19/).

Over the past seven years, the five-member group — Pablo, Stell, Josh, Ken, and Justin — has consistently challenged expectations, broken through barriers, and silenced every doubt thrown their way. Their journey hasn’t been an easy one, as it’s been marked by tireless work, criticism, and uncertainty. But through every setback, SB19 not only endured — for they thrived.

Together, they have consistently redefined what it means to be Filipino artists on a global stage, earning the hard-fought title of the “Kings of P-pop” — and proving with every performance why they deserve it. And with their [_Simula at Wakas_](https://open.spotify.com/album/04tWizEPzUimMQaZKdZwzJ?si=8y8QoK8CSee60LnteLoydw) kickoff concert, they proved it once again.

Despite relentless rain, fans showed up in droves at the Philippine Arena. Thousands queued from the early morning hours — not just for the music, but to honor a journey that belongs to both artist and audience. From the venue’s entrance to its bus terminals, SB19’s presence was everywhere. Dozens of buses wrapped in banners and portraits of Pablo, Stell, Josh, Ken, and Justin served as moving monuments to the group’s influence and the unshakable devotion of their fandom, [A’TIN](https://billboardphilippines.com/culture/scenes/what-it-took-atin-to-become-p-pops-most-famous-fandom-sb19-2024/ "The Making Of A’TIN, P-Pop’s Most Famous Fandom").

 ![Image 1](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/001-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 2](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/022-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 3](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/101-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

Before the show even began, a chorus of voices filled the arena for a spontaneous sing-along. Thousands of A’TIN members broke into song — “MAPA,” “Quit,” and “Crimzone” turned into arena-wide karaoke sessions, with their lightsticks flickering like stars. As I took in the moment, I realized just how raw, joyful, and affirming this concert was, for this was _their_ night too.

As the massive hourglass on the main screen counted down, a wave of energy coursed through the arena. From the moment the lights dimmed inside, one thing was made clear: SB19 wasn’t just about to perform; they were telling a story — one of struggle, success, and significance.

The opening was nothing short of cinematic — SB19 and their dancers emerged in red hooded robes, the thunderous instrumentals of “DAM” setting the stage for what would be an epic spectacle. Behind them, five colossal statues resembling each member loomed like deities — a declaration of legacy, power, and presence.

 ![Image 4](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/019-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 5](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/018-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 6](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/017-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 7](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/016-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

Once the robes came off, the show snapped into high gear. “What?,” “Mana,” and a freshly reimagined “Gento” hit back-to-back with electrifying force. SB19’s delivery was fierce and focused, commanding the stage with the precision of artists at the peak of their game. It was evident from these three tracks alone that the P-pop group wasn’t playing in our faces; rather, they were at their most empowered and inspired, bursting with a heightened energy that we haven’t seen before.

The evening seamlessly moved through both genres and moods. “Moonlight” and “I Want You” brought out a smoother, more sensual energy, where each member’s harmonies shone and vocals enveloped the arena in a dreamlike atmosphere. “Golden Hour” followed with rich emotional resonance, bringing a moment of calm amid the kinetic storm that raged beyond the arena’s walls.

 ![Image 8](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/006-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 9](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/081.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 10](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/047.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 11](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/096.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 12](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/079.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 13](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/086.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

Midway through the show, Pablo addressed the audience: “Sa mga pinapakita namin as SB19 \[With what we’ve shown as SB19\], know that everything is true, genuine, and from the heart_.”_ It was a powerful reminder of what has always set them apart — authenticity, depth, and honesty.

Such sincerity extended into every layer of the production. Visually, _Simula at Wakas_ was an artistic achievement. A symbolic flaming tree, a rocky mountain-shaped structure that surrounded the main stage, conceptual cinematic interludes, and an intricately designed extended stage that reached into the crowd all contributed to an immersive experience rarely seen in local concerts. For some reason, the massive size of the Philippine Arena (which stands as the world’s largest indoor venue) somehow felt intimate, thanks to SB19’s command of the space and the ingenious stage design that allowed members to interact closely with fans in all sections.

 ![Image 14](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/098-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 15](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/042-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 16](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/014-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 17](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/100-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

After a brief interlude, the group reignited the venue’s energy with “WYAT (Where You At).” High-octane and infectious, the track marked an electric turning point of the night, which was quickly followed by the pulsing beats of “DUNGKA!” and “BAZINGA.” To the benefit of those in attendance, these performances weren’t carbon copies of past shows as each member traded verses from their original renditions with their unique style, making every moment feel new, spontaneous, and personal.

It also reinforced their unmatched duality, which consisted of high-energy choreography, met together with crystal-clear live vocals. This synergy reached a peak with their debut live performance of the underrated “8TonBall” and a raucous run through “CRIMZONE” — a segment that not only spotlighted their stamina and talent but also showed the wild, unfiltered joy that SB19 still finds in performing. Even in a venue as massive as the Philippine Arena, they somehow made every corner feel seen and every person feel part of the moment, almost as if we were coming along for one wild, dance party too.

 ![Image 18](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/012.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 19](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/009.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 20](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/021-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 21](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/011-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 22](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/101-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

But what set _Simula at Wakas_ apart was its emotional depth. The setlist didn’t just flow — it told a story. After a stream of dance-driven anthems, the group turned inward with emotionally charged performances of “Nyebe,” “Time,” and “Quit.” These weren’t just slow songs — they were confessions. Showcasing not just their ever-growing vocal ability, but also their courage to be vulnerable in front of tens of thousands.

The atmosphere shifted further when Josh took the mic to share a deeply personal moment. With his voice shaking, he revealed that his father was present in the audience, watching him live for the first time. It was a vulnerable crack in the spectacle, and when “MAPA” played next, tears flowed across the arena, on stage and off. That performance became a shared memory between SB19 and A’TIN, marking a moment etched permanently in the emotional core of their story.

Not content to end on a somber note, the group shifted gears once more with a triumphant finale. The track run of “Shooting For The Stars,” “Freedom,” and “SLMT” erupted the arena with feelings of joy and gratitude. With several giant beach balls bouncing around the crowd, confetti raining down, and SB19’s members rising on an elevated platform to see the arena from above, the moment served as a symbolic vantage point, not of superiority, but of perspective.

 ![Image 23](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/002-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 24](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/091.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 25](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/080.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 26](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/045.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 27](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/084.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 28](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/041-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

“_Kahit ano mangyari, o ano pang gusto namin gawin, Isa lang gusto namin sabihin — salamat_” expressed Stell to the crowd, with his words clear, simple, yet ultimately deeply felt. \[“No matter what happens, or whatever we want to do in the future, there’s only one thing we’d like to tell you –– which is thank you.”\]

But SB19 still had one final exclamation point to make. A loud reprise of “DAM” closed the night, its pulsing intensity echoing louder than before. As smoke engulfed the stage and the symbolic tree burst into flames, the group exited like legends — not in silence, but in fire, fury, and triumph.

 ![Image 29](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/043-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 30](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/069-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 31](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/003-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

 ![Image 32](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/035-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

Even as the credits rolled, many A’TIN members were still wiping away tears. Because by the end of this _Simula at Wakas_ show, the message was undeniable. This wasn’t just a tour opener for their next shows over the next few months, nor was it just their biggest show to date. For it served as a chapter marker in OPM history — signaling how far SB19 has come, how deeply they’ve evolved, and how much more they have to give — building a new foundation for what’s to come.

The show captured the totality of their journey: whether it was the defiance of “DUNGKA!,” the vulnerability of “MAPA,” the joy of “SLMT,” and the ambition of “Shooting for the Stars.” Because each song was a stepping stone, and each moment was filled with meaning. Yet through it all, the bond between the group and their fans only deepened.

Few groups may be able to say that they’ve changed the course of an entire genre, but SB19’s _Simula at Wakas_ kickoff show was a moving reminder of how one group’s vision, grit, and talent have continued to push P-pop onto the world stage. All of it may have started with a dream, though it ended in a living legacy that’s still meant to continue.

Because as _Simula at Wakas_ proved once again, SB19 aren’t just making hits — they’re making history.

 ![Image 33: sb19 simula at wakas philippine arena concert billboard](https://billboardphilippines.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/005-1600x1066.jpg)

Photographed by Mayks Go

====================================================================

[Jan Milo Severo](https://www.philstar.com/authors/1805251/jan-milo-severo) - Philstar.com

May 27, 2025 | 4:00pm

[![Image 18: A 25x24 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://media.philstar.com/assets/icons/stroke-12-grey-comment.png)](https://www.philstar.com/entertainment/music/2025/05/27/2446203/sb19-partners-japanese-video-gaming-company-new-dungka-mv#comments)

![Image 19: SB19 partners with Japanese video gaming company for new 'Dungka' MV](https://media.philstar.com/photos/2023/07/25/1-1_2023-07-25_15-20-15.jpg)

SB19 members (from left) Justin, Stell, Pablo, Ken and Josh

SB19 via Instagram

ADVERTISEMENT

MANILA, Philippines — P-pop group SB19 partnered with SNK Corp., a renowned Japanese video gaming and interactive entertainment company.

A music video featuring SNK Corp. fighting game "Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves" and SB19 will be launched.

This partnership brings together two pop culture powerhouses in a creative fusion of music and gaming. The collaboration centers on SB19’s electrifying new banger “Dungka” inspired by the game’s key phrase, “REV IT UP.”

Combining the P-Pop group’s genre-defying sound with cinematic battle sequences from the beloved title, the music video captures the game’s exhilarating world and generates a whirlwind of excitement.

“We are truly honored to collaborate with a distinguished title celebrated for its sophisticated combat system and exceptional gameplay,” SB19 shared in an official statement. “As avid enthusiasts of interactive video games, we are thrilled by the opportunity to contribute to a project of this scale and significance. We extend our heartfelt gratitude to SNK Corporation for initiating this partnership and entrusting us with the chance to be part of such an iconic franchise. This collaboration has been an immensely rewarding experience, and we are sincerely grateful for its outcome.”

The collaborative effort coincides with the recent release of SB19’s third EP, “Simula at Wakas,” featuring one of the new singles “DUNGKA!” The 7-track collection offers a candid reflection on the personal and artistic journey of the group amid fame, pressure, and the search for identity. The EP is written and produced by SB19 with their trusted pool of international and local collaborators, including Xerxes Bakker, Alawn, August Rigo, Simon Servida, and Josue (RADKIDZ).

"Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves" is a 2025 fighting game published by SNK. It is the seventh main installment in the Fatal Fury series and the first new entry in 26 years, following "Garou: Mark of the Wolves" (1999). "Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves" features a unique art style that stimulates the senses, an innovative REV System that supercharges the excitement, plus a host of other battle systems even more robust than before.

Cristopher Diwata joins SB19 in unexpected collab for ‘DUNGKA’ dance challenge
==============================================================================

*   ![Image 6](https://pop.inquirer.net/wp-content/themes/taffees/images/unavailable-photo-default-final.png)[Xianna Bengo](https://pop.inquirer.net/byline/xianna-bengo)

*   [No Comments](https://pop.inquirer.net/376622/cristopher-diwata-joins-sb19-in-an-unexpected-collab-doing-the-dungka-dance-challenge#)
*   2.06K

 

SB19 had an unexpected collaboration with Cristopher Diwata, also known as the “What hafen, Vella” guy, on their TikTok video.

The viral internet personality and the P-pop kings danced together to the song “DUNGKA!”

![Image 8: SB19 Christopher Diwata](https://pop.inquirer.net/files/2025/05/SB19-Cristopher-Diwata.jpeg)

Screenshot

SB19 wrote in the caption, “Dungka with taylor laughter,” tagging Cristopher’s account.

> [@officialsb19](https://www.tiktok.com/@officialsb19?refer=embed) dungka with taylor laughter @Cristopher Diwata [#SB19](https://www.tiktok.com/tag/sb19?refer=embed) [♬ DUNGKA! – SB19](https://www.tiktok.com/music/DUNGKA-7490868129942849552?refer=embed)

“DUNGKA!” is an upbeat track that is part of the P-pop group’s much awaited EP “Simula at Wakas.” The said album also includes their comeback single, “DAM.”

People were delighted upon seeing the said video and took to the comments to express their thoughts on the unexpected collab.

One user wrote, “THE COLLAB WE DID NOT EXPECT WE NEEDED!! WUT HAFEN VELAAA?!!!”

Another user wrote, “Infairness, humble siya , kaya over flowing ang offer, usually kasi kahit trending di naman ganyan ang buhos ng blessing. Pawer sayo \[In fairness, he is humble, so the offer is overflowing, usually even thought it’s trending, the blessing are not like that. More power to you\]!”

A third user wrote, “Nakakatuwa na may ganito siyang exposure kasi talented din naman sya \[Happy that he has this exposure because he is also talented\].”

“Talented naman ni kuya, hahah kunin na ninyo ‘tong artista may potential \[Brother is talented, hahah get him as an artist he has a potential\],” a fourth user wrote.

![Image 10](blob:https://pop.inquirer.net/006ad7fa4b5f6d1e6d0af2a529c26ff3)

![Image 12](blob:https://pop.inquirer.net/4f84f4fe63ee3a4eb131263b19596d90)

Via TikTok

Aside from doing the dance challenge, the P-pop group also did their [version](https://vm.tiktok.com/ZShwMmWXd/) of the trend and also had a hilarious [skit](https://vm.tiktok.com/ZShwMQYAg/) with Cristopher.

Cristopher Diwata joined the “Kalokalike” segment on the noon-time show “It’s Showtime” as the look-alike of Hollywood actor Taylor Lautner. His “What hafen, Vella” monologue went viral 10 years after he joined the contest.

The P-pop kings will kick off their “Simula at Wakas World Tour” with a two-night concert at the Philippine Arena on May 31 and June 1.

They then would be having their tour across 18 cities in Asia, Middle East, and North America after their two-night kick off concert.
